introduction: Today the whole Church celebrates the dedication of the Lateran Basilica in Rome, the cathedral of the Pope as Bishop of Rome, and the mother and head of all churches. A feast of a building reminds us that we ourselves are God's temple. Ezekiel sees life-giving water flowing from the temple, and Jesus speaks of the temple of his body. Let us give thanks for our own church and for the living Church we form together.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, we are God's building, founded on Jesus Christ. Let us pray to the Father for the whole Church.
intentions: For the Pope, Bishop of Rome: that he may strengthen the faith of his brothers and sisters and guide the Church in unity. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our own parish church and all who serve in it: that it may be a house of prayer where everyone finds welcome. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christians whose churches have been destroyed or closed: that they may find strength in being living stones of God's temple. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are excluded or forgotten: that the life-giving water of the Gospel may flow to them through our charity. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may treat our bodies and our lives as temples of the Holy Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Father, you build your Church from living stones on the foundation of your Son. Make us a holy temple where your Spirit lives, and let your life flow through us to the world. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: God's temple is holy
reflection.body:
It may seem strange to keep a feast for a building. But the Lateran Basilica is the cathedral of Rome, and so the cathedral of the Pope. To celebrate it is to celebrate our unity with the Bishop of Rome and with the whole Catholic Church.

Ezekiel sees a vision of water flowing out from under the threshold of the temple. The stream grows deeper and deeper, and wherever it goes, it brings life: "everything will live wherever the river comes." Trees grow on its banks, "whose leaf won't wither, neither will its fruit fail." The temple is not a place where God's life is locked away, but a spring from which it flows out to the world.

In the Gospel, Jesus drives the merchants out of the temple: "Don't make my Father's house a marketplace!" When he is challenged, he says, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up," and John explains, "But he spoke of the temple of his body." The true temple is Christ himself, crucified and risen.

Paul draws the conclusion for us: "Don't you know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit lives in you?" We are "God's building," and the only foundation is Christ: "For no one can lay any other foundation than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ."

Our church buildings matter. They are where we are baptized, married, forgiven and fed. But they exist for the living Church, the people of God. This week, give thanks for the church where you worship, and ask how you can help it be a spring of life for the people around it.
